Samir —

Thanks for the clear asks. Below is a concise canary measurement plan we typically run for new customers migrating >50 QPS:

1) Canary windowing and sampling
   - Canary duration: 72 hours continuous; two 36-hour phases (baseline + warmed).
   - Measurement buckets: 5-minute sampling for p50/p95 aggregation into 1-hour rolling windows.
   - Sample inclusion: all production traffic directed to the canary instances; synthetic health probes excluded from SLO calc.
   - Minimum sample size: 10k requests per 1-hour window to consider the bucket representative; below that, we flag for noise.

2) Transient elevated p95 handling
   - Short bursts (<15 minutes): auto-fallback to regional-compatible model variant (lower compute) while preserving p50.
   - Medium bursts (15–180 minutes): temporary derating with grace policy — Redwood marks affected windows as provisional and performs a weighted rolling recalculation (70% historical, 30% canary) for 24 hours.

3) Canary-to-production cutover gate
   - Gate criteria: no hourly window with p95 > agreed threshold (e.g., 650ms) for two consecutive hours and no unmitigated error spike.
   - If gate fails: extend canary in 6–12 hour blocks and enable KV cache priming for hot prefixes.

I've attached a short runbook and a sample workbook showing the sample-count math. Lauren and Ben are cc'd to add operational controls (tracing hooks, alert thresholds). Happy to walk the SRE team through this in a 30-minute call.

kimberly
Kimberly Park

Samir / Kimberly —

Quick additions from an ops/observability perspective:

- Tracing and attribution: we recommend tagging the canary traffic with a canary_id header and instrumenting p95 by route + canary_id so you can split downstream traces quickly.
- Measurement signal: in addition to p50/p95, we compute a p99-lite (95th of 95th) for alerting on heavy tails during the canary.
- Evidence package: we'll produce a 72-hour report with per-hour windows, sample counts, and raw trace links. That package is what we use for any short-lived grace decision.

Ben — can you confirm the fallback model variants and whether the runtime can do automatic KV cache warmup on failover?

Lauren Bennett
Sr. Product Ops Manager, Redwood Inference

From: ben_carter@redwood.com
To: lauren_bennett@redwood.com, kimberly_park@redwood.com, Samir Rao <samir@fincloud.com>
Date: Mon, 18 May 2026 13:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Hosted API P50/P95 measurement — quick clarifications

Looping in a short technical confirmation:

- Fallback model variants: yes — our routing layer has pre-warmed compatible variants (smaller quantized variant) that can be promoted in <30s when p95 crosses the emergency threshold.
- KV cache warmup: automatic priming is supported; we can seed the cache with observed hot prefixes from the canary once the gate is passed or during an emergency failover we prime progressively from tiered storage.
- Sample size caveat: if FinCloud's initial traffic is very bursty and hourly windows drop below 10k requests, we recommend broadening to 4-hour aggregation to reduce false positives.

Ben Carter
Principal Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference

Samir —

Attached is a one-page addendum and an incident decision tree. Key bullets (so procurement can copy into the SOW):

- Provisional window definition: any 1-hour measurement window during the first 14 days post-cutover with sample size >= 5k and p95 > agreed threshold will be marked provisional. Provisional windows are excluded from SLA breach calculation for up to 72 hours while Redwood attempts automatic remediation. If remediation fails after 72 hours the window becomes binding.
- Weighted recalculation: provisional window value = 0.3 * observed_window + 0.7 * historical_hourly_median (historical median computed from the 7 days prior to cutover).
- Emergency fallback decision: auto-promote compatible variant when p95 exceeds emergency_threshold for two consecutive 5-minute buckets; on-call SREs are paged (pager duty group: infra-redwood) and can opt to roll back or approve manual promote.
- Ownership and evidence: Redwood will provide the 72-hour evidence package and an itemized change log; FinCloud retains final approval authority for production route switch.

I've scheduled the 30-minute walkthrough for Wed May 20, 11:00am PT — invite should hit your calendar shortly. Let me know if procurement wants tighter wording.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
